root.name: King's Gambit Accepted: MacLeod Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 Nc6

overview: Black develops the queenside knight instead of the usual ...g5 or ...d6, keeping the f4 pawn for now. White typically plays 4.d4 to build the centre with a free hand against a delayed Black plan, and the game is open and tactical. I am not sure of the exact main line, but it is a rare King's Gambit Accepted sideline.

white_ideas.idea: Build the centre with d4 and Bc4 or Nc3, then regain the f4 pawn or attack on the f-file
Use the open f-file and development lead to attack f7

black_ideas.idea: Develop the knight and hit the centre with ...d5 or ...g5 depending on White's move
Keep the extra pawn if possible and return it when needed to complete development

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with the f-file half-open and Black f4 pawn under pressure

character.notes: King's Gambit lines are open with exposed kings; the MacLeod is double-edged.

gambit.notes: Black has the f4 pawn and can try to keep it with ...g5 or ...d6 and ...Be7.

soundness.notes: Probably sound, but I am not certain about the main line.

approach.notes: Strong players play King's Gambit rarely, MacLeod a sideline of it; but not unknown.

level.notes: King's Gambit lines require knowing the theory and tactics; I am unsure about this branch.

character.reason: A King's Gambit with exposed kings and open lines.

gambit.reason: White gives the f-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Playable for both sides as far as I know.

approach.reason: A sideline of an accepted gambit that strong players sometimes play.

level.reason: Some theory is needed, but it is not a deep forcing tree.

plans.reason: White gives a pawn for development and the attack on the king.
